newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends down, May fails above $22.00.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends down, May fails above $22.00.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures ended lower Friday after the new front-month May contract failed to hold above $22.00 early in the session.
"It was choppy. (May crude futures) made a run up above $22.00 but couldn't sustain the gains. I'm eyeing $21.20 support," said Thomas Blakeslee, a trader at Cargill Investors Service.

The market was knocked back by a story suggesting more Iraqi oil output might be on the horizon, but was bounced a bit by an uncomfirmed report of trouble at one of Venezuela's smaller refineries, traders said.

Russia's fuel and energy minister Pyotr Rodionov, while signing a $3.5 billion oilfield development deal earlier Friday in Baghdad, said Russia would pursue the deal despite the United Nations sanctions which restrict dealings with the Baghdad regime.

However, oil experts said it was unclear whether the Russian minister really meant to imply sanctions busting or that the deal would be like those signed by France in the past, which are contingent on a lifting of sanctions.

Meanwhile, the possibility of a shortage of gasoline in California if a threatened strike proceeds against three Uncocal refineries scheduled to be taken over by Tosco Corp helped to lift gasoline futures in New York early on, but those gains faded by the close.
April gasoline moved up to a high of 68 cents a gallon but settled just 0.06 higher at 67.64 cents.
April heating oil settled 0.04 higher at 55.98 cents a gallon.
